newsitem.title: USA: NationsBank in talks to buy Boatmen's - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: NationsBank in talks to buy Boatmen's - WSJ.

text.p: NationsBank Corp, in a move that could create a financial giant stretching from Maryland to New Mexico, is in talks to buy Boatmen's Bancshares Inc in a deal worth about $9.5 billion, The Wall Street Journal reported Friday.

The agreement would move NationsBank closer to its vision of being a nationwide institution. Now operating in nine states, mainly in the South and Washington D.C., the Charlotte, N.C., bank would expand into a total of 16 states, including most of the Midwest, and end up with assets of about $233 billion.

NationsBank, the United States' fifth-biggest banking company, is expected to pay about $60 to $61 in a combination of cash and stock for each Boatmen's share. That would represent a premium of 41 percent above Boatmen's closing price of $42.9375 in Thursday trading on the Nasdaq Stock Market.
Boatmen's, based in St. Louis, has about 157.4 million shares outstanding.
A combination of NationsBank with Boatmen's Midwestern franchise could spark another wave of banking industry consolidation, the newspaper said.
Boatmen's has been a frequently touted takeover target, especially since last year when a federal banking statute stripped the company of state regulatory protection.
